scope: Functional McKernel OS/apps and Rust/assembly migration only; no security testing.
accepted_source_delta: transfer_image: failed page-transfer ioctl now returns-1 immediately after the existing diagnostic, preventing later pages/sections and false success.

act_execve: nonzero phase2 result retains main_loop_ret, invokes existing command-server cleanup, then existing exit_process(1). This avoids the worker-return path whose td.ret is discarded by join_all_threads.

lifetime_and_error_review.caller: SYS_EXECVE reaches act_execve through act_main_loop_syscall. act_execve_phase2 propagates transfer_image failure before image-ok, CLOSE_EXEC, cloexec handling or success RET.
lifetime_and_error_review.cleanup: The candidate uses the same cleanup/process-exit bridge sequence as act_exit. The inspected bridge calls exit(term); no signature or bridge implementation changes are proposed.
lifetime_and_error_review.locking: The inspected Rust caller and failure branch introduce no held lock, join or new allocation across cleanup. Real optional command-server shutdown behavior is not established by the mocks.
lifetime_and_error_review.ownership: Fatal exit does not itself prove host/guest response, descriptor, physical-memory or OS retirement. Those obligations remain with the matched provider and existing owner lifecycle.
lifetime_and_error_review.ABI_geometry_sentinel: The exact diff contains only the two stated changes. Transfer descriptor ABI, direction, page geometry, sentinel logic and success ordering remain unchanged.

actual_body_evidence.observed_failure_order: perror,image-failed,cmd-cleanup,process-exit1; no later page/section or success events
actual_body_evidence.compile_warning_scope: Two private_interfaces warnings caused by the harness-private McexecSyscallWaitDesc type used by extracted public functions. Warning stream retained; target compilation is not proved.

source_eligibility: Eligible for the next matched launcher build under existing strict build controls.
limitations: Mocks establish selected propagation and ordering, not real command-server cleanup, multithreaded exit behavior, kernel resource release or native exec.
Cases cover two aligned full-page sections and first/second-page failure; no additional geometry or failure-branch coverage is inferred.
Existing allocation/descriptor-transfer/error-RET branches were unchanged and receive no new acceptance.
Matched target build/link acceptance, host exec-transfer provider, fresh release and actual native failure/success retirement remain necessary.
